findings.claim: Of 43 room names, 16 read CONTRADICT on served fundamentals. The commonest pattern is a stalwart priced like a fast grower: P/E 34-56 on 0-7% EPS growth (A, TMO, DHR, FAST, EW, TAK, KDP, HLT). Lynch PEG > 2 is a red flag (C8).
findings.evidence: A pe=34 eps3y~+3%; TMO pe=36.5 eps flat; DHR pe=38 eps -5/-17/-34; FAST pe=42 peg~8; EW pe=51; HLT pe=53 eps 0%

findings.claim: The room's top-tallied name (3 seats) has the weakest growth under the price: three years of 0-7% revenue and 1-5% EPS growth at P/E 34, at a 52-week high after +47.6% in 6 months. Momentum is real; the business story does not explain it.

Four hotel REITs are in the room: one cyclical story counted four times. Two of them have losses (PEB, PK) and SHO's EPS fell two straight years. PEB is up 95% in 12 months on flat 2% revenue. NAV and debt kind are unserved, so the asset-play case cannot be tested.
findings.evidence: PEB 12m=+95% rev+2% npm-3%; PK npm-6% dy6%; SHO eps -70/-85%; DRH eps +144% rev flat

findings.claim: These names doubled or tripled while revenue was flat or shrinking. That is the 'hot stock in a hot industry' shape Lynch warns about: the price is running ahead of anything the income statement shows.

These are the names whose figures support the price. AVPT and FRSH have clean balance sheets (de<=0.04) and 16-27% sales growth at sensible multiples. TDC (FCF yield ~24%) and CRBG (~12%) pass the C13 cash test. TDC's shrinking sales is the open question.
findings.evidence: AVPT rev+27/22/17 de0.04; FRSH p/fcf15.5 rev+16/21/20; TDC pe6.6 p/fcf4.1; CRBG p/fcf8.5 dy2.8%

findings.claim: Six names show negative book equity, so the C12 equity-ratio test cannot pass as computed. For HLT, MTCH and CAH this is buyback-driven, a known pattern. For W, EQH and PBI it comes with losses or shrinking sales. The kind of debt (C15, bank vs funded) is unserved.
findings.evidence: pb: W -5.4, HLT -13, MTCH -45, CAH -21, PBI -2.7, EQH -19

findings.claim: For these names TTM GAAP P/E misstates the business. DT's P/E of 127 is tax-distorted. ESTC and FRSH report net margins well above operating margins, so profit is coming from non-operating items. MRK's P/E of 118 sits on a 5% net margin. Read them on P/FCF, and have the PM verify one-offs.
findings.evidence: DT pe127 p/fcf33; ESTC opm-1% npm21%; FRSH opm3% npm20%; MRK pe117.7 npm5%

findings.claim: MP is a held turnaround with negative gross margin (-4.6%), operating margin of -33% and negative FCF, at 21.5% under its SMA. Under C22, an add is warranted only if the story is verified intact, and served data cannot verify that. Survival liquidity (cash, debt maturities) is unserved. The broker stop of 36.66 is deferred to house law (C21); this is not an argument against it.

Calendar context (C23): the window is now October-December tax-loss season, but the room is mostly at or near 52-week highs. The depressed names are MP (held, -21.5%), ENB (-17% from high), TRP (-12%) and KR (-15%). This is advisory only; it is not a nomination.
findings.evidence: pct_from_52w_high: ENB -17.28, KR -15.17, TRP -12.13; MP sma -21.48

findings.claim: For the energy cyclicals, XOM's P/E (22.9) has expanded while its EPS fell for three years, so the price is discounting a commodity turn. Commodity futures vs spot and capacity build (C18) are unserved. EOG has the cleanest figures of the three.
